verdict.rationale: LM Studio ships its own server mode that exposes local models on OpenAI-like endpoints, locally and over the network. It also has a headless daemon (llmster) and an Anthropic-compatible POST /v1/messages endpoint, which together make it a plausible agent backend. However, no evidence names a coding agent connected to it or shows that working end-to-end, so the coding-agent part of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: documented coding-agent integration guides, evidence of tool-calling reliability for agent loops, hands-on reports of a coding agent running against LM Studio.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect a coding agent to this product as a working backend

citations.quote: Serve local models on OpenAI-like endpoints, locally and on the network

Headless mode, or "Local LLM Service", enables you to leverage LM Studio's technology (completions, chat completions, embedding, structured outputs via `llama.cpp` or `Apple MLX`) as local server powering your app.
The headless LM Studio flow is especially nice because it makes local inference usable from real tools instead of as a demo.
